explanation: The clay army was buried with China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huang, who died in 210 BC. Farmers digging a well found it in 1974.

claims.text: The Terracotta Army was made for the tomb of Qin Shi Huang and buried around 210 BC.
The Venus de Milo was carved around 150 to 125 BC.
Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor of a unified China, died in 210 BC.
Farmers digging a well near Xi'an discovered the Terracotta Army in 1974.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Venus de Milo: The Louvre's own collection record dates it to 150–125 BC, in the third quarter of the 2nd century BC, and labels it Hellenistic (Date: Epoque / période : hellénistique Date de création/fabrication : 3e quart IIe s. av. J.-C. (-150 - -125)). Other scholars give somewhat different ranges. Wikipedia describes the modern consensus as the 2nd century BC, perhaps between 160 and 110 BC.

claimResults.note: Tier A: the summary names the Louvre's own collection record, 150 to 125 BC. Wikipedia's wider 160 to 110 BC consensus contains that range, so it does not contradict 'around 150 to 125 BC'.
